test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The status of Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna to the Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) is conferred by:

options.text: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Department of Public Enterprises**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) under the Ministry of Finance grants the status of Maharatna, Navratna, and Miniratna to Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)
 
• The DPE plays a key role in developing policies and guidelines for the performance and functioning of public sector enterprises in India
 
• To be eligible for Miniratna category I status, a CPSE must meet the following criteria:
 
 
• Have made profits continuously for three years 
 
• Have a pre-tax profit of at least Rs. 30 crores in at least one of the three years 
 
• Have a positive net worth
 
 
 
• This categorization allows CPSEs to enjoy greater autonomy and authority in financial and operational matters, supporting their growth and competitiveness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs
 
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) primarily focuses on maintaining internal security, law and order, and administering Union Territories.
 
• It also coordinates between various state governments on national security issues but has no role in conferring the Maharatna, Navratna, or Miniratna status to CPSEs, as these statuses are economic and administrative designations rather than security-related.
 
 
 
• The Ministry of Commerce and Industry
 
 
• The Ministry of Commerce and Industry promotes trade, industry, and exports to drive economic growth and development.
 
• It focuses on policies related to foreign trade, foreign direct investment (FDI), and industrial regulation. 
 
 
 
• The Department of Private Enterprises
 
 
• There is no Department of Private Enterprises within the Government of India.
